name: Moon

landmark.label: Lane crater

researchNotes: The Moon is tidally locked: we always see the same near side. The far side was first imaged by Luna 3 (1959) and mapped in detail by later orbiters.
Lane crater sits on the far side near the equator. It is named for Jonathan Homer Lane (1819–1880), astrophysicist linked to Hampton Falls, New Hampshire.
Phases change with the Sun–Moon–Earth angle. Synodic month is about 29.5 days — the rhythm behind tonight's moon phase on the dome.
folklore: Moon lore and werewolf tales are storytelling. The crater name Lane is an IAU scientific dedication, not folklore.
carlFocus: Lead with Lane crater and Jonathan Homer Lane when asked. Cover phases, tidal locking, and Apollo / LRO facts. Offer the Lane Museum link.
